hypotheses: At rho=0, guardrail selection (C) reduces metered traffic and wasted work; its final-window accuracy is similar to or better than random selection (A).
As rho increases, guardrail selection (C) becomes less representative of profile-linked classes; random over-selection (B) may improve coverage at higher resource cost.
Policy D's staleness bonus should reduce participation imbalance among eligible vehicles without violating guardrails.
Connectable peer pairs may show class-coverage bias when parked Wi-Fi availability correlates with usage profile.
